api-server.title: API Server
api-server.description: Node.js/Express REST API. Handles authentication (JWT/bcrypt), CRUD on notes, file uploads to MinIO. Bridges the frontend and backend networks. Single most security-critical component — compromise equals full data access.
api-server.justification_cia_rating: The API processes all user data. It bridges both Docker networks — a compromised API container can pivot into the internal data tier.

communication_links.title: Redis Session Store
communication_links.description: Session token storage and JWT revocation list. Password-protected (requirepass) but no TLS.

communication_links.title: MinIO File Storage
communication_links.description: INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: S3 API calls to MinIO over plain HTTP. Default minioadmin/minioadmin credentials are hardcoded in compose. Any container on backend-net can read all stored files.

communication_links.title: PostgreSQL Connection
communication_links.description: Application-level SQL queries for user auth, notes CRUD. Uses parameterized queries (pg library) to prevent SQL injection. No TLS on the connection — traffic is plaintext within backend-net.

browser-spa.title: Browser SPA
browser-spa.description: React Single Page Application served from Nginx. Users authenticate, manage notes, and upload files through this interface.
browser-spa.justification_cia_rating: Client-side code is public; the trust boundary here is user data entered into the browser. XSS would allow an attacker to exfiltrate session tokens.

communication_links.title: HTTPS to Nginx
communication_links.description: User-initiated HTTPS requests carrying credentials (login) and note content (create/edit). This is the only encrypted link in the chain.

minio-storage.title: MinIO Object Storage
minio-storage.description: S3-compatible object store for file attachments. INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: Uses default minioadmin/minioadmin credentials (visible in docker-compose.yml) and stores files without encryption at rest. HTTP-only (no TLS) within the Docker network.
minio-storage.justification_cia_rating: Stores user file uploads which may contain sensitive documents. Default credentials + no encryption = trivial exfiltration by any process on backend-net.

nginx-proxy.title: Nginx Reverse Proxy
nginx-proxy.description: Nginx terminates TLS and forwards all API traffic to the Express server over plain HTTP (port 3000). This is the DMZ entry point.

technologies.name: reverse-proxy
technologies.description: A proxy hiding internal infrastructure from caller making requests. Can also reduce load

nginx-proxy.justification_cia_rating: Nginx is the single external entry point. Its compromise exposes all downstream services. Availability is critical — outage = full service outage.

communication_links.title: HTTP to API Server
communication_links.description: INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: Traffic between Nginx and the API server uses plaintext HTTP. An attacker with access to the Docker network (container escape, compromised sidecar) can intercept credentials, session tokens, and note content in transit.

postgresql-db.title: PostgreSQL Database
postgresql-db.description: Primary relational datastore. Contains users table (email + bcrypt password hash), notes table (title + content), and attachments metadata. INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: No encryption at rest (encryption: none).
postgresql-db.justification_cia_rating: Holds all user PII (email, hashed passwords) and all note content. Strictly confidential — unencrypted disk access exposes all data.

redis-cache.title: Redis Cache
redis-cache.description: In-memory store used as session store and JWT revocation list. INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: No encryption at rest. If Redis persistence is enabled and the RDB file is exfiltrated, session tokens are exposed.
redis-cache.justification_cia_rating: Session token exposure enables account takeover. Non-persistent by default but the container volume could persist RDB snapshots.
